issues.problem: The link is cited as support for the claim that an exception test must assert the specific expected type and fail on no exception or a different one. The fetched excerpt covers general unit-test benefits and the Fast/Isolated/Repeatable/Self-Checking traits and shows nothing about exception assertions, Assert.Throws or catch-all handlers. The generator notes also admit the page may not discuss this. The Assert.Throws<T> claim in the explanation is correct, but nothing in the item backs it.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace or supplement the link with a page that documents the claim, for example the xUnit assertions documentation for Assert.Throws<T> / ThrowsAny<T>. Alternatively, cite the best-practices page only for the self-checking trait and drop the implication that it covers exception assertions. Update linkTitles in ru and en to match.

issues.problem: The excerpt is cut off just before the try-catch section. It does show a `catch (Exception e)` example and the CLR looking for a compatible catch block, which is enough to support that catch (Exception) catches everything. The fact that every exception derives from Exception is not stated in the visible text.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the link. Optionally soften the explanation to "catch (Exception) matches any exception".

The Fowler excerpt ("be aware with static data and singletons") supports the isolation and order-dependence point. The xUnit instance-per-test detail is not in the cited sources.
